references.text: During the Passover festival in Jerusalem, many believed in Jesus' name when they saw the signs he performed. The Galileans who welcomed Jesus had seen exactly this ([ref:Joh 2:23|John 2:23]).
Jesus' journey to Jerusalem in connection with the Passover feast, which is the festival referred to in this verse ([ref:Joh 2:13|John 2:13]).

The immediate context: Jesus left Samaria for Galilee after saying that a prophet is not honored in his own homeland. The reception of Jesus by the Galileans here stands in contrast to that statement ([ref:Joh 4:43-44|John 4:43-44]).

The Mosaic law commanded all men to appear before the Lord three times a year, including during the Feast of Unleavened Bread (Passover). This explains why the Galileans were present in Jerusalem during the festival ([ref:5 Mos 16:16|Deut 16:16]).

Shortly afterward, Jesus warns that people will not believe unless they see signs and wonders, which sheds light on the Galileans' reception—it was based on what they had seen, not necessarily on genuine faith ([ref:Joh 4:48|John 4:48]).
Nicodemus confirms that Jesus performed signs in Jerusalem, supporting the fact that Jesus' deeds there were well known ([ref:Joh 3:2|John 3:2]).
